## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

- productivity:task-management: Simple task management using a shared TASKS.md file. Reference this when the user asks about their tasks, wants to add/complete tasks, or needs help tracking commitments.
- productivity:update: Sync tasks and refresh memory from your current activity. Use when pulling new assignments from your project tracker into TASKS.md, triaging stale or overdue tasks, filling memory gaps for unknown people or projects, or running a comprehensive scan to catch todos buried in chat and email.
- cowork-plugin-management:cowork-plugin-customizer: Customize a Claude Code plugin for a specific organization's tools and workflows. - cowork-plugin-management:create-cowork-plugin: Guide users through creating a new plugin from scratch in a cowork session. This skill requires Cowork mode with access to the outputs directory for delivering the final .plugin file.
- small-business:ad-manager: The ads consultant that becomes an ads agent. Reads paid-ad performance natively through the TikTok Ads connector, or via a build-connector Zapier connection for other ad platforms, explains in plain English what is working and what is burning money, recommends budget, targeting, and creative changes with the dollar impact of each, drafts new ad copy in the owner's voice plus Canva creative briefs, and — only after an explicit yes — executes the approved changes in the ad account. Works from exported CSV reports when nothing is connected, the normal starting point. Use this whenever the owner talks about ads or ad spend at all, including "are my ads working," "what's my ROI on ads," "I'm spending money on Facebook and I don't know what I'm getting," "should I turn this campaign off," "my cost per lead is going up," "write me a new ad," "who should I be targeting," or "the ad guy quit."
- small-business:ap-processor: Works the bill pile end to end: reads bills and vendor statements out of the AP inbox or from uploaded PDFs and phone photos, pulls out vendor, amount, due date, and line detail, codes each one to the right account and job, matches it against the purchase order and the receiving ticket, then stages the entries and a proposed payment run in QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite for the owner to approve in one pass. Nothing is entered and nothing is paid without an explicit yes. Reach for this whenever bills, vendor invoices, or paying people comes up — including "what do I owe," "the bills are piling up," "pull the invoices out of my email and into QuickBooks," "code these for me," "who needs to get paid this week," "did we get billed twice," or when the owner forwards a supplier invoice with no message at all. Use it before cash-flow-snapshot or month-end-prep so those run on real payables instead of a guess.
- small-business:brand-style: Sets and updates the owner's brand look and output preferences, which every page and document the plugin produces then follows automatically. Captures the brand from a pasted website link or a plain-words description — never a hex code, color picker, or upload — previews it on a sample page, asks how they want their outputs delivered (visual artifacts, Word docs, markdown, Notion pages, Canva Docs, or best-for-the-skill), and saves both to the business profile. Runs inside smb-onboard on first setup and stands alone forever after. Use when the owner says "update my brand," "we rebranded," "change my colors," "make the reports match our new look," "change how you give me reports," "I want Word docs instead," or anything about the look or format of what the plugin hands them.
- small-business:build-agent: Turns a task the owner keeps doing by hand into a named, reusable skill they can trigger by name or put on a schedule. Watches them do it once or listens to them describe it, works out what varies and what stays fixed, writes the skill with approval checkpoints in the right places, registers it with the router, and shares it with the team. This is how a business gets a workflow nobody shipped for them. Use this whenever the owner describes something repetitive they wish were automatic — including phrasings like "I do this every week," "can you remember how to do this," "make this a thing I can just ask for," "build me an agent," "automate this for me," "turn this into a workflow," or "I want this to happen every Monday." Reach for it when they describe a routine, even without asking for automation.

Use this whenever the owner names a tool that isn't connected — including phrasings like "can you connect to my," "make my tools talk to each other," "there's no API for this," "pull data out of my field service software," "I use ServiceTrade and it's not on the list," or "is there any way to get at this data." - small-business:canva-creator: Takes an approved content brief and executes a campaign end-to-end: builds the posting calendar, generates Canva designs for social posts, drafts caption and email copy, and stages social sends in HubSpot. Every step requires explicit owner approval. This is the one-shot campaign executor: a finished brief goes in, a complete campaign comes out. Use when the owner hands off an approved brief or points at one — "run this brief," "execute the campaign," "turn this brief into posts," "build the campaign from the plan we approved." Use when the user says "review this contract," "what am I signing," "red flags," "flag any concerns," "check the payment terms," or uploads/forwards a contract or legal agreement.

Runs on demand or on a schedule, includes a hygiene sweep for duplicates and stale records, and builds a lightweight CRM in a spreadsheet for owners who don't have one. Use this whenever the owner mentions email at all — including "drowning in email," "I have 300 unread," "what emails need me," "go through my inbox," "clean up my email," "did I miss anything," "who am I supposed to get back to," "draft a reply to this," or "catch me up on my mail." Flags the money sitting still too — overstock, dead stock, and zero-velocity items, reported as slow movers to clear rather than things to buy more of. Seasonality is applied where the history supports it and named where it does not. Nothing is ordered and no vendor is emailed without approval. Reach for this whenever stock comes up — "what do I need to reorder," "am I going to run out," "what should I order this month," "we keep running out of filters," "how much cash is sitting in the warehouse," "what is not moving," or "draft a PO for my supplier."
- small-business:invoice-chase: Drafts overdue-invoice reminder emails from the ledger (MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books) plus PayPal, Stripe, and Airwallex data, matched to each customer's payment history and tone (gentle for good customers, firm for repeat late payers). Works out the owner's ideal customer profile from the customers they already have, finds look-alike companies and the right contact at each, enriches them with firmographics and buying signals, scores them, and delivers the list as an XLSX, with an offer to also create the records in the CRM. Use this whenever the owner wants new prospects, a target list, or help finding customers — including phrasings like "who should I be calling," "find me more customers like my best ones," "build me a prospect list," "I need leads," "who else looks like Acme," or "help me find companies in this area that need what we do." - small-business:lead-triage: Scores inbound HubSpot leads by engagement signals, company fit, and urgency markers, ranks the ones worth a call today with talking points, drafts the follow-ups, and proposes calendar times for the owner to book. An ask that wants the ranked leads turned into a call list with time blocked on the calendar routes to /call-list, which runs this skill first and then books the time.
- small-business:marketing-monday: Delivers the weekly growth briefing as one merged read — whether the growth engine is working, what customers are saying in public and private, what competitors actually changed, and the three growth actions worth taking this week. Use this whenever the owner wants a recurring or one-off growth check, including phrasings like "how's marketing doing," "growth check for the week," "give me my Monday growth brief," "what should I be doing about growth this week," "are we winning or losing out there," or "set up a weekly marketing update." Reach for it when the owner asks how the business is growing rather than how it is paying its bills.

- small-business:ap-processor: Works the bill pile end to end: reads bills and vendor statements out of the AP inbox or from uploaded PDFs and phone photos, pulls out vendor, amount, due date, and line detail, codes each one to the right account and job, matches it against the purchase order and the receiving ticket, then stages the entries and a proposed payment run in QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite for the owner to approve in one pass. Nothing is entered and nothing is paid without an explicit yes. Reach for this whenever bills, vendor invoices, or paying people comes up — including "what do I owe," "the bills are piling up," "pull the invoices out of my email and into QuickBooks," "code these for me," "who needs to get paid this week," "did we get billed twice," or when the owner forwards a supplier invoice with no message at all. Use it before cash-flow-snapshot or month-end-prep so those run on real payables instead of a guess.
- small-business:brand-style: Sets and updates the owner's brand look and output preferences, which every page and document the plugin produces then follows automatically. Captures the brand from a pasted website link or a plain-words description — never a hex code, color picker, or upload — previews it on a sample page, asks how they want their outputs delivered (visual artifacts, Word docs, markdown, Notion pages, Canva Docs, or best-for-the-skill), and saves both to the business profile. Runs inside smb-onboard on first setup and stands alone forever after. Use when the owner says "update my brand," "we rebranded," "change my colors," "make the reports match our new look," "change how you give me reports," "I want Word docs instead," or anything about the look or format of what the plugin hands them.
- small-business:build-agent: Turns a task the owner keeps doing by hand into a named, reusable skill they can trigger by name or put on a schedule. Watches them do it once or listens to them describe it, works out what varies and what stays fixed, writes the skill with approval checkpoints in the right places, registers it with the router, and shares it with the team. This is how a business gets a workflow nobody shipped for them. Use this whenever the owner describes something repetitive they wish were automatic — including phrasings like "I do this every week," "can you remember how to do this," "make this a thing I can just ask for," "build me an agent," "automate this for me," "turn this into a workflow," or "I want this to happen every Monday." Reach for it when they describe a routine, even without asking for automation.
- small-business:build-connector: Gets Claude talking to a tool nobody built an official connector for. Works out what the system is, checks the Claude connector directory for an existing connector first, and when there isn't one connects the tool through Zapier — never by hand-building against a raw API — with credentials handled safely and approval gates on anything that writes. This is what turns "my ERP isn't supported" into an afternoon. Use this whenever the owner names a tool that isn't connected — including phrasings like "can you connect to my," "make my tools talk to each other," "there's no API for this," "pull data out of my field service software," "I use ServiceTrade and it's not on the list," or "is there any way to get at this data." Reach for it whenever an unsupported system is blocking something else.
- small-business:business-pulse: Produces a one-page cross-functional business snapshot for SMB owners — cash position (the ledger: MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books), sales trend (PayPal/Square/Stripe), pipeline movement (HubSpot), this week's commitments (Calendar), urgent watch-list items (Gmail or M365, Slack), and the single most important thing needing attention today. Proactively tries every available connector and gracefully scopes to whatever is connected — one connector gives a partial pulse; the full stack gives the full picture. Trigger when the user asks how the business is doing, wants a snapshot, a daily brief, a Friday recap, or says anything like "what am I missing" or "catch me up on the business." A start-of-week briefing routes to /monday-brief, which runs this skill as its first link.
- small-business:call-list: Builds today's call list. Runs lead-triage to rank the top-5 leads most worth calling, supplies talking points from email history, blocks time on the calendar, and drafts follow-up messages. Trigger on "call list," "who am I calling today," "top five to call today," or "block time for calls." An owner who wants leads scored or ranked with no calendar blocks routes to lead-triage directly. Accepts optional count and date arguments.
- small-business:canva-creator: Takes an approved content brief and executes a campaign end-to-end: builds the posting calendar, generates Canva designs for social posts, drafts caption and email copy, and stages social sends in HubSpot. Canva is used for social posts only (Instagram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn) — email content is drafted as plain text and surfaced inline for the owner to send from their own tool. Every step requires explicit owner approval. This is the one-shot campaign executor: a finished brief goes in, a complete campaign comes out. Use when the owner hands off an approved brief or points at one — "run this brief," "execute the campaign," "turn this brief into posts," "build the campaign from the plan we approved." For day-to-day posting with no brief — "I need to post more," "what should we post" — use social-content-engine instead; it owns the standing calendar.
- small-business:cash-flow-snapshot: Reads AR/AP, historical cash timing, and known fixed costs from the ledger (MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books) or from PayPal, Square, or Stripe — or a CSV upload — and produces a 30/60/90-day cash flow forecast with percentage-variance confidence bands and named risk flags. Delivers a chat summary and a downloadable XLSX. Use when the user asks "forecast my cash flow," "will I make payroll," mentions "runway," or says "cash crunch." Falls back to CSV upload when no connector is live.
- small-business:close-month: Closes the books and turns them into a decision as a three-link chain — month-end-prep reconciles the ledger against every connected payment processor and writes the P&L narrative, cash-flow-snapshot then refreshes the 30/60/90-day forecast off the newly closed numbers rather than raw ones, and report-builder publishes and distributes the close packet. Requires a ledger (MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books) and uses Gusto, PayPal, Ramp, Shopify, Square, and Stripe when connected, falling back to statement or CSV uploads. Trigger on "close the month," "month-end," "close the books," "reconcile," "send the close packet to my accountant," or when the owner asks why revenue or margin moved last month. An owner who wants only the reconciliation and its flags, with no forecast refresh and no packet distribution, routes to month-end-prep directly.
- small-business:content-strategy: Analyzes sales data from PayPal and QuickBooks to find top performers and slow movers, layers in seasonality, and produces a prioritized 30-day content brief: what to push, what offers to run, what to hold. Strategic output only — no calendars or assets. Use when the user asks what to post, wants a content plan, asks what's selling, or what to promote this month.
- small-business:contract-review: Lightweight NDA, MSA, and vendor contract review for SMBs without legal on staff. Reads contracts from local files, mail attachments (Gmail or M365), a connected file store (Google Drive or M365), or DocuSign envelopes; flags non-standard terms; explains risks in plain English; and outputs a marked-up redline as a separate DOCX. Use when the user says "review this contract," "what am I signing," "red flags," "flag any concerns," "check the payment terms," or uploads/forwards a contract or legal agreement.
- small-business:crm-autopilot: Keeps the CRM current without the owner ever opening it. Creates and updates contacts and deals from email, calendar, and call transcripts; logs activity automatically; drafts follow-ups on deals that have gone quiet; and maintains a next-step queue so nothing sits unowned. Runs on demand or on a schedule, includes a hygiene sweep for duplicates and stale records, and builds a lightweight CRM in a spreadsheet for owners who don't have one. Use this whenever CRM data or pipeline hygiene comes up — including phrasings like "update my CRM," "log this call," "clean up HubSpot," "clean up Salesforce," "add this to the deal," "turn my meeting into a deal note," "which deals have gone quiet," "I hate data entry," or "my pipeline is out of date." Reach for it when the owner describes a call or meeting worth recording, even without naming the CRM.
- small-business:grant-rfp-writer: Finds grant and solicitation opportunities the organization actually qualifies for, runs a hard go/no-go before anyone starts writing, drafts the application or response from past submissions and real program data, and tracks every deadline and reporting obligation that follows an award. Built for nonprofits, government contractors, and education, and it filters daily feeds like SAM.gov or DIBBS down to the handful worth bidding. Runs on Google Drive or M365 with DocuSign and Calendar deepening it, and works from uploaded past submissions plus web research when nothing is connected. Use this whenever a funding or bidding opportunity is in play — including "find grants we qualify for," "should we bid this," "draft the response to this RFP," "we've got 50 solicitations to filter," "what's due on the federal grant," or "help me write the proposal narrative."
- small-business:grow-pipeline: Fills the funnel end to end without the owner babysitting it — reads the market and the competition for context, builds a ranked list of named prospects with a reason attached to each, writes personalized outreach in the owner's own voice, and logs every touch to the CRM. Chains lead-finder, outreach-composer, and crm-autopilot behind a web-native market read, with an owner approval at every handoff. Use this whenever the owner wants more pipeline rather than one specific piece of it, including phrasings like "I need more leads," "fill my funnel," "who should I be calling and what do I say," "find me customers like my best ones and reach out," "build me a prospect list and write the emails," or "sales has gone quiet, get something moving." Reach for it when the owner describes wanting new business generally rather than asking for a list or a single email.
- small-business:growth-pulse: Answers one question for an SMB owner — is the growth engine actually working? Pulls sales trend by channel, funnel conversion, campaign return, best and worst performing products, and customer sentiment from whatever is connected, then ends with the three growth actions worth taking this week. The growth-side twin of business-pulse, which covers the finance side. Use this whenever the owner asks how marketing or sales is performing, whether a campaign paid off, where leads are coming from, why the pipeline is stalling, which products are moving, or says anything like "is my marketing working," "growth check," "how's the funnel," or "where should I put my money next month." Reach for it even when the owner names a single channel rather than growth overall.
- small-business:hiring-screener: Takes a pile of applications and turns it into a ranked shortlist, scored only against the job's stated rubric, with drafted replies to every candidate, scheduled interviews, and an onboarding checklist for whoever gets hired. Picks up where job-post-builder leaves off and carries the funnel through to first day, including the payroll setup handoff. Runs on Gmail and Google Calendar, deepens with Gusto, DocuSign, and Drive or M365, and works entirely from uploaded resumes with drafted replies the owner sends by hand. Use this whenever the owner has applicants to deal with — including phrasings like "I've got 40 resumes and no time," "who should I interview," "screen these applications," "help me narrow this down," "set up interviews for the top three," or "I need to tell the rest no." Reach for it when the owner mentions applicants, resumes, candidates, or being buried in a hiring inbox.
- small-business:inbox-manager: Turns a full inbox into a short, ranked list of what actually needs the owner. Reads the mail, sorts it into needs-you, drafted-and-waiting, and handled, writes replies in the owner's own voice, pulls out the action items and deadlines buried in long threads, files what is finished, and hands bills, leads, and scheduling requests to the skills that own them. Works from pasted or forwarded email text when no mailbox is connected. Use this whenever the owner mentions email at all — including "drowning in email," "I have 300 unread," "what emails need me," "go through my inbox," "clean up my email," "did I miss anything," "who am I supposed to get back to," "draft a reply to this," or "catch me up on my mail." Reach for it for one forwarded message as readily as for a whole morning's backlog.
- small-business:inventory-planner: Works out what to reorder and when, from what is actually selling: pulls sales history and stock on hand from Shopify, Square, NetSuite, or an uploaded CSV, computes 7-day and 28-day sales velocity per item, projects a conservative stockout date for each, sizes a 60-day reorder quantity, and drafts the purchase orders and vendor emails to cover it. Flags the money sitting still too — overstock, dead stock, and zero-velocity items, reported as slow movers to clear rather than things to buy more of. Seasonality is applied where the history supports it and named where it does not. Nothing is ordered and no vendor is emailed without approval. Reach for this whenever stock comes up — "what do I need to reorder," "am I going to run out," "what should I order this month," "we keep running out of filters," "how much cash is sitting in the warehouse," "what is not moving," or "draft a PO for my supplier."
- small-business:invoice-chase: Drafts overdue-invoice reminder emails from the ledger (MYOB, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Zoho Books) plus PayPal, Stripe, and Airwallex data, matched to each customer's payment history and tone (gentle for good customers, firm for repeat late payers). Sends via PayPal with owner approval; everything else queues as a mail draft, with the Airwallex hosted pay link included where one exists. Use when the user asks "who owes me money," mentions overdue invoices, or wants to follow up on unpaid invoices.
- small-business:job-post-builder: Builds end-to-end hiring packets — job post, structured interview guide with scoring rubric, and offer letter template — from a hiring brief. Triggers on: "help me hire", "we're hiring for", "write a job post", "job description", "JD", "open role", "create a job ad", "interview questions", "scoring rubric", "draft an offer letter", "send an offer", "make a hiring packet", or any request to recruit for a position. When in doubt, trigger — covers the full hiring workflow from job post through DocuSign envelope creation via browser. Does NOT screen or rank applicants.
- small-business:lead-finder: Builds a ranked list of prospects worth contacting. Works out the owner's ideal customer profile from the customers they already have, finds look-alike companies and the right contact at each, enriches them with firmographics and buying signals, scores them, and delivers the list as an XLSX, with an offer to also create the records in the CRM. Runs on Apollo when connected and falls back to web research plus an uploaded customer list when it isn't. Use this whenever the owner wants new prospects, a target list, or help finding customers — including phrasings like "who should I be calling," "find me more customers like my best ones," "build me a prospect list," "I need leads," "who else looks like Acme," or "help me find companies in this area that need what we do." Reach for it even when the owner describes the customer they want rather than asking for a list.
- small-business:lead-triage: Scores inbound HubSpot leads by engagement signals, company fit, and urgency markers, ranks the ones worth a call today with talking points, drafts the follow-ups, and proposes calendar times for the owner to book. Use when the owner asks to prioritize, score, or rank leads, asks "who should I call first," or asks about their pipeline. An ask that wants the ranked leads turned into a call list with time blocked on the calendar routes to /call-list, which runs this skill first and then books the time.
- small-business:marketing-monday: Delivers the weekly growth briefing as one merged read — whether the growth engine is working, what customers are saying in public and private, what competitors actually changed, and the three growth actions worth taking this week. The growth twin of the Monday brief, chaining growth-pulse and review-reputation and adding a web-native competitor scan, merged into a single page rather than three reports. Offers to run on a weekly cadence once, and sets it up on a yes. Use this whenever the owner wants a recurring or one-off growth check, including phrasings like "how's marketing doing," "growth check for the week," "give me my Monday growth brief," "what should I be doing about growth this week," "are we winning or losing out there," or "set up a weekly marketing update." For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

# BMW Product Management Challenge (TUM.ai Hackathon Final)

## Mission
Build an AI-powered platform that helps BMW product managers (PMs) derive, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements for the successor** of an existing vehicle line, 3 to 5 years ahead. It ingests BMW data plus web research, turns it into cases (problems) and requirements (solutions), prioritizes them with explainable logic, keeps the PM in control, and records everything in an audit trail.

The platform is generic: vehicle and market are configuration. The demo shows at least one derivative in one market.

BMW values: trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, clear handling of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, evidence vs. assumption made explicit.

## Scope
**In:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as experienced by the customer, variant and package offering.
**Out:** regulatory / homologation, technical / engineering specs, pricing and business case (cost or effort only as a rough prioritization factor).

## Deliverables
1. Concept + demonstrable prototype.
2. Sample requirement list. Each requirement: unique ID, clear actionable description, linked signals and sources, priority / score, prioritization rationale, evidence level, future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, decision status.
3. End-to-end workflow: what the AI does autonomously, where human review is mandatory.
4. Audit trail: source, signal, consolidation, scoring, prioritization, human decision. Records changes to content, scores, priorities, evidence and status with actor (AI or human), timestamp and rationale.

## Repository map
- `README.md`: short project overview.
- `plan.md`: approved implementation plan (phases 0 to 10). Progress table and open issues at the top.
- `architecture.mmd`: target architecture (Mermaid). **Source of truth for the pipeline.**
- `database-design.md`: database design (tables, columns, rules) for Supabase Postgres + pgvector. **Source of truth for tables and fields.**
- `data-model.mmd`: diagram of `database-design.md` (Mermaid ER).
- `changes.md`: every decision changed during implementation, with reason and who decided.
- `taxonomy/`: the fixed taxonomy (11 car areas, 219 topics, 11 aspect groups), its build script and the classifier eval. **Source of truth for the classification.** Only a human changes it.
- `backend/`: the brain (FastAPI, migrations in `backend/supabase/migrations/`, tests in `backend/tests/`). Run tests with `cd backend && uv run pytest` (embedded local Postgres, no network).
- `backend/reports/`: generated reports (clustering thresholds, fetch plan, end-to-end runs with audit chains).
- `backend/API.md`: how the UI calls the API (auth, errors, main flows); the OpenAPI spec at `/docs` is the contract.
- `web/`: the UI (Next.js). Its REST contract is `web/src/contracts`; `web/src/backend` is the adapter that serves this contract from the API (`DATA_SOURCE=backend`), `web/src/mock` the synthetic demo data (default, offline fallback). The two are never mixed.
- `HANDOFF.md`: state of the work, decisions of the last session, what is not verified, what to do next. Read after this file.
- `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`: the gap analysis between UI and backend. Finished; kept as a record.
- `layers.mmd`: BMW's process slide as a diagram, for reference only (not our architecture).
- `All-context/README.md`: index of all material. Read first.
- `All-context/01-challenge/`: briefing, mission sheet, BMW process slides (md transcriptions + original PDF/PNG).
- `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/`: provided data. Its `README.md` documents columns, counts and caveats.
- `All-context/03-meetings-with-pm/`: meeting summaries and notes, transcripts in `raw/`. **The two PM interviews are the primary user research.**
- `All-context/04-team-notes/`: early brainstorm (superseded by the architecture where they differ), original in `raw/`.
- `All-context/05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md`: web sources, fetch order and record format for the fetch agents (owned by a teammate).

## Provided data (short)
| Dataset | Vehicles | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| Customer feedback (xlsx, 3 files) | F70 1 Series, G60 5 Series, G70 7 Series | Free-text English verbatims, classified by type (Likes, Difficult to Use, Defect, Wants) and topic. One row per topic, so count unique IDs. F70: 2,128 verbatims, UK/JP, ICE only. G60 and G70: 4,000 each, ~90% US, ICE/PHEV/BEV. - PMs today use benchmarking, customer studies, social listening, sentiment reports and car clinics. Tools: Excel, PowerPoint, Jira, Confluence, SharePoint. **Research is the bottleneck.**

Versioned JSON with exact quote (must be found in the stored source record), short English summary (≤ 20 words), market, topic, aspect group, car area, vehicle role, author hash and reach. Invalid signals go to a visible quarantine.

- **Aspect group** (11, grouped from VFC level 3): function, usability, reliability, performance, efficiency_range, design, comfort, space, quality, sound, price. Neutral, so likes and complaints share a group. `price` is tagged out of scope and stays visible.
- **Car area** (11): what the PM sees and filters by. Always derived from the topic in code, never predicted.
- BMW rows get topic and aspect group by lookup from their VFC labels; rows labelled `no_class_found` or general enquiry are classified from the text. Web signals: the LLM picks from the closed lists (strict enums).

- Usually groups many signals, each linked to its quote and source.
- Holds all opinions (complaints, wishes, likes), counted per market and powertrain, so market conflicts become visible.
- **Not tied to one vehicle.** A problem can come from several BMW lines and series (shared Baukasten features, the My BMW app). The vehicles it applies to are tags (`case_vehicle`); lifecycle state, PM rank and release fit are per vehicle, because each line has its own PM. Case IDs carry no vehicle (`CASE-0012`); the table is `case_item` (`CASE` is reserved in SQL).
- **Owned per line.** A case has an owner, co-owners and watchers per line. Only the owner, a co-owner or the head of product line changes it; the first PM who works an unowned case becomes its owner; anyone may escalate to the head. Handing a case to another PM or pulling it from the innovation pool never copies it: the same case then applies to the receiver's line.
- Card texts written with the page: a short title (2 to 4 words), a summary and three highlights (problem, who, competition). AI tags also cover case type and change depth.
- Figures: distinct customers, reach (capped), study satisfaction, equipment today (standard / optional / absent), competitor offer, trend.
- Tags: vehicles, scope, brand fit, segment (AI proposes, PM can override).
- **No cost.** A problem has no cost.
- Importance score from case factors weighted by the PM's weight profile; PM can override the rank by dragging, with a reason.
- Lifecycle (per vehicle): **observed** (auto-clustered, overview map only) → **open** (threshold reached: enough distinct customers, a defect, a competitor gap or a removed feature; or opened by the PM) → **confirmed** or **rejected** by the PM after meetings and discussion. Rejected cases stay with their reason.
- While a case is open the PM moves it through a **workflow** step (new, investigating, awaiting answers, ready). The PM's decision is the **outcome**: confirmed, rejected, merged, or, with the case staying open, referred to another PM, sent to the innovation pool or parked.

- After confirmation the daily loop still attaches new signals, but the case never changes by itself; it gets a flag ("+40 complaints since confirmation").

- Generated by the requirement agent only after the PM confirms a case. In the UI the PM first answers at most three shape questions (scope, benchmark, release, solution, offer); the agent drafts with the PM's context: the series brief (layer 1), the stance on the case (layer 2), the shape answers (layer 3). Feedback from engineering or finance (layer 4) leads to a proposed new version.
- Structured fields are the source of truth (short title, description by sentence, metrics with basis and benchmark, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope, release, cost); the page is rendered from them. Every part carries its provenance: evidence (with signal IDs), PM context (with the layer) or assumption. Every content change is a numbered version with its cause.
- One per confirmed case and BMW line (`REQ-G60-0012`). Several only when markets differ clearly: then one per market (`REQ-G60-USA-0012`).
- Content: description; metric and target based on today's value (seed) and competitor values; acceptance criteria; release target (next generation, current car update, OTA software); assumptions and uncertainties; evidence level (BMW data / web / assumption, display only, not in the score); link to its case and through it to every signal and source.
- **Cost lives here**: option price if it exists, else an AI estimate S / M / L; PM and engineers edit it.
- Editable with engineering: PM and engineers edit, re-target or delete (delete = tombstone in the audit log). Same Notion-like page with RAG sidebar.
- Rank = case score x cost multiplier (S 1.0, M 0.85, L 0.7); PM can override by dragging.
- Status flow: draft → in discussion → approved (by the PM) → signed off (by the head of product line, who can also send it back) → planned (on the vehicle plan) → exported. The approved top 10 go to engineering.

## Pipeline (steps in `architecture.mmd`)
0. **Configuration:** vehicle + market (valid only if sales > 0), competitor set (default, AI suggests, PM confirms), brand profile (versioned assumption, PM-editable), source filter, several weight profiles per vehicle with a compare view.
1. **Seed (one-time, logged):** option lists (extracted once by the team and verified, page as source), portfolio (segment, generation, markets), sales (2030 forecast = market weight), customer study (raw + normalized 0..1 + US dissatisfied share), BMW feedback Excel converted to signals (car area via topic mapping), the fixed taxonomy as the feature catalog (one feature per topic), with option codes and study attributes mapped to topic IDs (these two mappings confirmed by the team). Predecessor-generation research only on demand when the PM flags a removed feature.
2. **Daily fetch loop:** Python worker + cron, four agents (competitor, customer/public feedback, trends, innovation scout), daily budget (500 requests) with priority (features with open cases first, rest rotates), cadence per source (forums, app reviews, news daily; reviews and complaint sites weekly; reference and market data monthly). Reddit is not used (API access needs an approved developer application). Sources, categories A to J and record format: `fetching-sources.md` (sections 3 and 7). Scope v1: fetch-order steps 1 to 9 (steps 10 to 13 later). Depth: one backfill over all pages, then daily incremental runs that stop at already-stored records. A general search provider is only needed for discovery and stays pluggable.
3. **Signal JSON + validation gate:** schema, stored record, quote found, duplicates, source filter, dated competitor facts. Rejected → quarantine (PM can delete: content purged, tombstone kept). Agents pick topic and aspect group from the fixed taxonomy; the car area is derived from the topic (no separate classifier). Older-generation signals kept and tagged. Original quote + English translation for non-English sources. Schema has fixed core fields + `extra`, versioned.
4. **Cases:** group signals by topic + aspect group ("Seats + comfort" and "Seats + reliability" are separate cases); only large groups are split further by similarity (summary embeddings, OpenAI embeddings, threshold tuned on seed data), never across a topic. Stable IDs, merges/splits logged. Figures and tags per case. Conflict flag when one market is mostly negative and another mostly positive, each with ≥ 5 distinct customers (PM-tunable).
5. **Case score** (no cost), computed per weight profile, so per config (vehicle + market), from the signals of that vehicle; defaults: distinct customers 0.25, severity 0.20, satisfaction gap 0.15, competitor gap 0.15, market volume 0.10, removed vs predecessor 0.05, reach 0.05 (capped, log, per market), trend 0.05; brand fit multiplier (fits 1.0, neutral 0.8, off-brand 0.5). Rationale text generated from the factor breakdown.
6. **PM workspace:** notification toast (new open case, new evidence, conflict, failed run), case board, case page with RAG sidebar, PM confirms case.
7. **Requirement generation** from confirmed cases (see concept above).

End filters on the case and requirement boards: market, car area / category, state, source type, and **release fit** (current car update, next generation, OTA), judged by an LLM from how big the case is; the PM can override.
8. **Requirement ranking, discussion with engineering, approval.** Export format (codebeamer / Jira) is a later feature.

## Technical decisions

- The RAG agent also knows the PM context (series briefs, stances, open questions and answers, meeting notes, feedback, comments) through its own tool; it cites it as PM context, never as customer evidence, and uses only the brief of the asking PM's line.
- AI proposals are rows of `proposal` (seven kinds); a person accepts or rejects each, and accepting applies the change through the object's own audited endpoint.
- Collaboration lives in the database, all audited: series briefs (one shared per line plus a regional overlay per PM), stances, open questions, meeting notes, referrals and escalations, innovation pool, comments, alerts, the vehicle plan (a plan feature is a topic; only the PM's decisions are stored).
- Users: `app_user.role` is the permission (pm, engineer, admin); `pm_role` is the place in the organisation (vehicle PM, attribute PM, head of product line). Each user has a workspace: one config (vehicle and market) and one weight profile.
- Pages: markdown body stored in the DB with versions; structured fields (score, status, market, cost) separate; stale saves rejected by version check.
- UI (Notion-like pages, boards) is built by a teammate; the backend provides data, scores and the RAG agent. The UI keeps its own vocabulary (markets EU / US / CN / RoW, release `lci`, status `pm_approved`); the adapter translates, the database keeps the backend values.
- Text shown to a person in the UI is readable prose ("Status: planned → exported"), never raw JSON.
- YouTube: videos of the last 60 days on the listed review channels, the 10 most relevant comments per video, BMW lines only (quota). Transcripts come through an unofficial library and can be blocked.

- A separate confidence axis in the score (evidence level is display only).
- A graph database.
- A separate car-area classifier step (Jev); the car area is derived from the topic.
- Loading the database from the processed CSVs (`docs/02-data/processed`); it is loaded from BMW's original files, which keep the sheet and row of every value.
- Deleting BMW feedback rows that are not relevant; they are kept out of cases, scores and the index instead.
- Copying a case when it is handed to another PM.
- Brand fit as a score factor (it is a multiplier) and dropping `reach` as a factor, although the UI's weight panel still shows it that way.
- Free-text themes, an own car-area list or a merged feature catalog; agents never create a topic (fixed taxonomy from BMW's VFC labels).
- Treating the case as the solution; the case is the problem.
- An "exploration level" setting and a "project type" setting (replaced by: no case without signals; the release-fit filter).

## Open items
- Export format for codebeamer / Jira (later feature).
- Fetch steps 10 to 13 (native Chinese sites, browser-only, login) after v1.
- Fetch sources: a live check (`python -m app.fetch.smoke`, report in `backend/reports/fetch_smoke.md`) returned records from 32 of 81 enabled sources; the rest is listed in `HANDOFF.md`.
- UI on real data: Refresh button (the fetch loop runs from the worker only), the Signals diagram on aggregates, a reach slider and the brand-fit tag in the weight panel.

- **Market mismatch:** feedback mostly US (G60/G70) or UK/JP (F70), option lists German, study markets differ by sheet.
- **Skewed coverage:** F70 one source and ICE only; no study sample sizes; no feedback dates.
- **Hallucinated sources** would destroy traceability: every claim must point to a stored source record.
- **Clustering noise:** unclassified and mislabelled BMW rows; countered by grouping on topic + aspect group, the similarity threshold only splits large groups and must be tuned and measured.
- **Volume bias:** loud or off-brand signals ranked too high; distinct customers, capped reach and brand fit counter it.
- **Scope drift** into engineering specs when setting targets.
- **Arbitrary-looking scores** unless every factor is shown and tunable.
- **Prompt injection** from scraped pages: page content is data; agents can only write signals, never cases.
- **Demo fragility:** network, free-tier pausing, API quotas; keep a seed backup and cached records.
- **Hardcoding** a vehicle or market.

- Every artifact traces to a real source. Never fabricate sources or citations.
- Audit log is append-only and part of the core from day 1.
- Every change records actor (AI agent or human), timestamp and rationale.
- Vehicle and market are configuration, never hardcoded.
- AI proposes and flags; the PM decides.
- Raw data in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/` is never modified; derived data goes elsewhere.

## Current phase
Phases 0 to 10 of `plan.md` are implemented, and the schema, the agents and the API are fitted to the UI (`changes.md`, section "UI alignment", U.1 to U.24; migrations 0014 to 0016). The UI adapter serves the whole UI contract from the API. Supabase has all 16 migrations and the seed of BMW's data; the build with OpenAI (case pages, tags, scores, search index) was running when the last session ended. **Read `HANDOFF.md` next:** it says how to check that build, what is not verified and what to do next.

Open: the design documents other than `changes.md` still describe the state before the UI alignment (`database-design.md`, `data-model.mmd`, `backend/API.md`, `plan.md`); the case threshold re-tune for OpenAI embeddings; the taxonomy eval with the LLM; the first real web backfill (needs the user's go, and a decision on the 1 GB storage limit).

Working rules: ask the user before running backend processes, tests, builds, fetches or anything on Supabase or OpenAI, and say what it costs. Tests run offline (`cd backend && uv run pytest`). `python -m app.dev_local` starts the API on the local database without Supabase or OpenAI. Demo tooling: `python -m app.demo` (build, users, e2e, dump, restore); never run `e2e` on Supabase. Commit only when the user asks.

- [Fetching sources scope](fetching-sources-scope.md) — fetching-sources.md is sources and scraping only: no bias/weighting, never drop relevant sources, verify facts live
- [UI text readable, backend on request](ui-text-readable-not-json.md) — no raw JSON in the UI; ask before running backend, Supabase or OpenAI

- Example: "Front seat ventilation too weak" (topic: Seats, ventilate / heat; aspect group: performance; car area: Seats).
- Usually groups many signals, each linked to its quote and source.
- Holds all opinions (complaints, wishes, likes), counted per market and powertrain, so market conflicts become visible.
- **Not tied to one vehicle.** A problem can come from several BMW lines and series (shared Baukasten features, the My BMW app). The vehicles it applies to are tags (`case_vehicle`); lifecycle state, PM rank and release fit are per vehicle, because each line has its own PM. Case IDs carry no vehicle (`CASE-0012`); the table is `case_item` (`CASE` is reserved in SQL).
- **Owned per line.** A case has an owner, co-owners and watchers per line. Only the owner, a co-owner or the head of product line changes it; the first PM who works an unowned case becomes its owner; anyone may escalate to the head. Handing a case to another PM or pulling it from the innovation pool never copies it: the same case then applies to the receiver's line.
- Card texts written with the page: a short title (2 to 4 words), a summary and three highlights (problem, who, competition). AI tags also cover case type and change depth.
- Figures: distinct customers, reach (capped), study satisfaction, equipment today (standard / optional / absent), competitor offer, trend.
- Tags: vehicles, scope, brand fit, segment (AI proposes, PM can override).
- **No cost.** A problem has no cost.
- Importance score from case factors weighted by the PM's weight profile; PM can override the rank by dragging, with a reason.
- Lifecycle (per vehicle): **observed** (auto-clustered, overview map only) → **open** (threshold reached: enough distinct customers, a defect, a competitor gap or a removed feature; or opened by the PM) → **confirmed** or **rejected** by the PM after meetings and discussion. Rejected cases stay with their reason.
- While a case is open the PM moves it through a **workflow** step (new, investigating, awaiting answers, ready). The PM's decision is the **outcome**: confirmed, rejected, merged, or, with the case staying open, referred to another PM, sent to the innovation pool or parked.
- Notion-like page (markdown body + structured fields) with a RAG sidebar agent that discusses, cites sources and proposes edits as diffs the PM accepts or rejects.
- After confirmation the daily loop still attaches new signals, but the case never changes by itself; it gets a flag ("+40 complaints since confirmation").

**Requirement = the answer to a confirmed case.** What BMW will build or change, customer-facing and measurable, no engineering specs.
- Generated by the requirement agent only after the PM confirms a case. In the UI the PM first answers at most three shape questions (scope, benchmark, release, solution, offer); the agent drafts with the PM's context: the series brief (layer 1), the stance on the case (layer 2), the shape answers (layer 3). Feedback from engineering or finance (layer 4) leads to a proposed new version.
- Structured fields are the source of truth (short title, description by sentence, metrics with basis and benchmark, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope, release, cost); the page is rendered from them. Every part carries its provenance: evidence (with signal IDs), PM context (with the layer) or assumption. Every content change is a numbered version with its cause.
- One per confirmed case and BMW line (`REQ-G60-0012`). Several only when markets differ clearly: then one per market (`REQ-G60-USA-0012`).
- Content: description; metric and target based on today's value (seed) and competitor values; acceptance criteria; release target (next generation, current car update, OTA software); assumptions and uncertainties; evidence level (BMW data / web / assumption, display only, not in the score); link to its case and through it to every signal and source.
- **Cost lives here**: option price if it exists, else an AI estimate S / M / L; PM and engineers edit it.
- Editable with engineering: PM and engineers edit, re-target or delete (delete = tombstone in the audit log). Same Notion-like page with RAG sidebar.
- Rank = case score x cost multiplier (S 1.0, M 0.85, L 0.7); PM can override by dragging.
- Status flow: draft → in discussion → approved (by the PM) → signed off (by the head of product line, who can also send it back) → planned (on the vehicle plan) → exported. The approved top 10 go to engineering.

## Pipeline (steps in `architecture.mmd`)
0. **Configuration:** vehicle + market (valid only if sales > 0), competitor set (default, AI suggests, PM confirms), brand profile (versioned assumption, PM-editable), source filter, several weight profiles per vehicle with a compare view.
1. **Seed (one-time, logged):** option lists (extracted once by the team and verified, page as source), portfolio (segment, generation, markets), sales (2030 forecast = market weight), customer study (raw + normalized 0..1 + US dissatisfied share), BMW feedback Excel converted to signals (car area via topic mapping), the fixed taxonomy as the feature catalog (one feature per topic), with option codes and study attributes mapped to topic IDs (these two mappings confirmed by the team). Predecessor-generation research only on demand when the PM flags a removed feature.
2. **Daily fetch loop:** Python worker + cron, four agents (competitor, customer/public feedback, trends, innovation scout), daily budget (500 requests) with priority (features with open cases first, rest rotates), cadence per source (forums, app reviews, news daily; reviews and complaint sites weekly; reference and market data monthly). Reddit is not used (API access needs an approved developer application). Sources, categories A to J and record format: `fetching-sources.md` (sections 3 and 7). Scope v1: fetch-order steps 1 to 9 (steps 10 to 13 later). Depth: one backfill over all pages, then daily incremental runs that stop at already-stored records. A general search provider is only needed for discovery and stays pluggable.
3. **Signal JSON + validation gate:** schema, stored record, quote found, duplicates, source filter, dated competitor facts. Rejected → quarantine (PM can delete: content purged, tombstone kept). Agents pick topic and aspect group from the fixed taxonomy; the car area is derived from the topic (no separate classifier). Older-generation signals kept and tagged. Original quote + English translation for non-English sources. Schema has fixed core fields + `extra`, versioned.
4. **Cases:** group signals by topic + aspect group ("Seats + comfort" and "Seats + reliability" are separate cases); only large groups are split further by similarity (summary embeddings, OpenAI embeddings, threshold tuned on seed data), never across a topic. Stable IDs, merges/splits logged. Figures and tags per case. Conflict flag when one market is mostly negative and another mostly positive, each with ≥ 5 distinct customers (PM-tunable).
5. **Case score** (no cost), computed per weight profile, so per config (vehicle + market), from the signals of that vehicle; defaults: distinct customers 0.25, severity 0.20, satisfaction gap 0.15, competitor gap 0.15, market volume 0.10, removed vs predecessor 0.05, reach 0.05 (capped, log, per market), trend 0.05; brand fit multiplier (fits 1.0, neutral 0.8, off-brand 0.5). Rationale text generated from the factor breakdown.
6. **PM workspace:** notification toast (new open case, new evidence, conflict, failed run), case board, case page with RAG sidebar, PM confirms case.
7. **Requirement generation** from confirmed cases (see concept above).

End filters on the case and requirement boards: market, car area / category, state, source type, and **release fit** (current car update, next generation, OTA), judged by an LLM from how big the case is; the PM can override.
8. **Requirement ranking, discussion with engineering, approval.** Export format (codebeamer / Jira) is a later feature.

## Technical decisions
- Storage: Supabase Postgres + pgvector, relational with link tables (no graph DB). Raw records in storage, referenced by `raw_ref`.
- Audit: append-only event table enforced in the DB (no update / delete); actor (AI agent or PM), timestamp, before/after, rationale; views and exports logged too. Deletions are tombstones.
- Field names and market values follow `fetching-sources.md` section 7: markets `USA`, `China`, `Europe`, `Rest of World`, `unknown`; `vehicle_role` current / predecessor / competitor / unknown; `author_hash` for distinct web customers.
- LLM: OpenAI models. gpt-6-luna for everything high-volume (row classification, signal extraction, case pages, case tags, RAG sidebar), gpt-6.1-sol only for requirement texts (`OPENAI_STRONG_TASKS`). Thinking effort: `low` for the reading tasks (classification, signal extraction, case pages, case tags; `OPENAI_MINIMAL_REASONING_TASKS`), the model's default for the RAG sidebar and the requirement texts. Every agent output stores model and prompt version.
- Embeddings: text-embedding-3-small stored with 768 dimensions (`EMBEDDING_DIM`). No vector index on `signal` and `rag_chunk` (exact search at this size); see the size budget below.
- The LLM never works inside a database transaction: a batch step reads, closes the transaction, lets the calls run in parallel (`LLM_WORKERS`) into the disk cache `backend/.data/llm_cache/` (key = prompt version + model + thinking effort + inputs), then writes in a short transaction.
- Size budget: Supabase free plan, 500 MB database and 1 GB storage. Observed cases are not scored (a case is scored when it opens); machine events are not indexed for the RAG agent; a fetched web record without a relevant statement keeps only a marker row. BMW's provided data is never dropped: irrelevant rows are kept out of cases, scores and the index (quarantine, out of scope), not deleted.
- RAG agent: hybrid keyword + vector search over case and requirement pages, signals with quotes, source records, decisions and audit events of people. Every factual claim cites a signal ID; no source means "no evidence found". Edits are proposals the PM accepts.
- The RAG agent also knows the PM context (series briefs, stances, open questions and answers, meeting notes, feedback, comments) through its own tool; it cites it as PM context, never as customer evidence, and uses only the brief of the asking PM's line.
- AI proposals are rows of `proposal` (seven kinds); a person accepts or rejects each, and accepting applies the change through the object's own audited endpoint.
- Collaboration lives in the database, all audited: series briefs (one shared per line plus a regional overlay per PM), stances, open questions, meeting notes, referrals and escalations, innovation pool, comments, alerts, the vehicle plan (a plan feature is a topic; only the PM's decisions are stored).
- Users: `app_user.role` is the permission (pm, engineer, admin); `pm_role` is the place in the organisation (vehicle PM, attribute PM, head of product line). Each user has a workspace: one config (vehicle and market) and one weight profile.
- Pages: markdown body stored in the DB with versions; structured fields (score, status, market, cost) separate; stale saves rejected by version check.
- UI (Notion-like pages, boards) is built by a teammate; the backend provides data, scores and the RAG agent. The UI keeps its own vocabulary (markets EU / US / CN / RoW, release `lci`, status `pm_approved`); the adapter translates, the database keeps the backend values.
- Text shown to a person in the UI is readable prose ("Status: planned → exported"), never raw JSON.
- YouTube: videos of the last 60 days on the listed review channels, the 10 most relevant comments per video, BMW lines only (quota). Transcripts come through an unofficial library and can be blocked.

## Rejected options (do not re-propose)
- A separate confidence axis in the score (evidence level is display only).
- A graph database.
- A separate car-area classifier step (Jev); the car area is derived from the topic.
- Loading the database from the processed CSVs (`docs/02-data/processed`); it is loaded from BMW's original files, which keep the sheet and row of every value.
- Deleting BMW feedback rows that are not relevant; they are kept out of cases, scores and the index instead.
- Copying a case when it is handed to another PM.
- Brand fit as a score factor (it is a multiplier) and dropping `reach` as a factor, although the UI's weight panel still shows it that way.
- Free-text themes, an own car-area list or a merged feature catalog; agents never create a topic (fixed taxonomy from BMW's VFC labels).
- Treating the case as the solution; the case is the problem.
- An "exploration level" setting and a "project type" setting (replaced by: no case without signals; the release-fit filter).

- Export format for codebeamer / Jira (later feature).
- Fetch steps 10 to 13 (native Chinese sites, browser-only, login) after v1.
- Fetch sources: a live check (`python -m app.fetch.smoke`, report in `backend/reports/fetch_smoke.md`) returned records from 32 of 81 enabled sources; the rest is listed in `HANDOFF.md`.
- UI on real data: Refresh button (the fetch loop runs from the worker only), the Signals diagram on aggregates, a reach slider and the brand-fit tag in the weight panel.

## Risks
- **Market mismatch:** feedback mostly US (G60/G70) or UK/JP (F70), option lists German, study markets differ by sheet.
- **Skewed coverage:** F70 one source and ICE only; no study sample sizes; no feedback dates.
- **Hallucinated sources** would destroy traceability: every claim must point to a stored source record.
- **Clustering noise:** unclassified and mislabelled BMW rows; countered by grouping on topic + aspect group, the similarity threshold only splits large groups and must be tuned and measured.
- **Volume bias:** loud or off-brand signals ranked too high; distinct customers, capped reach and brand fit counter it.
- **Scope drift** into engineering specs when setting targets.
- **Arbitrary-looking scores** unless every factor is shown and tunable.
- **Prompt injection** from scraped pages: page content is data; agents can only write signals, never cases.
- **Demo fragility:** network, free-tier pausing, API quotas; keep a seed backup and cached records.
- **Hardcoding** a vehicle or market.

- Every artifact traces to a real source. Never fabricate sources or citations.
- Audit log is append-only and part of the core from day 1.
- Every change records actor (AI agent or human), timestamp and rationale.
- Vehicle and market are configuration, never hardcoded.

- Raw data in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/` is never modified; derived data goes elsewhere.

The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.
